question.problem:
Consider the binomial random variable $X∼B(6,0.65).$ Rounding to $4$ decimal places, fill in the missing value in the cumulative distribution function table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $P(X\le x)$ | $0.0018$ | $0.0223$ | $0.1174$ | $0.3529$ | $0.6809$ | {{field-1}} |
question.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

The probability mass function for the Binomial distribution $B(n,p)$ is given by

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},\,x=0,1,2,…,n.
$$

In our case, $n=6$ and $p=0.65.$ 

Therefore, we compute the missing element of the table as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(5) & =P(X\le 5) \\  & =P(X\le 4)+P(X=5) \\  & =F(4)+P(X=5) \\  & =0.6809+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{5})(0.65)^{5}(1-0.65)^{6-5} \\  & =0.6809+6\cdot (0.65)^{5}\cdot (0.35)^{1} \\  & ≈0.9246.\end{aligned}
$$
